Thanks Lena — confirmed for Tue 10:00 PT. Quick technical notes ahead of the call so we're efficient:

1) VPC peering vs Private Endpoint (summary)- VPC peering: simple, low operational overhead, requires non-overlapping CIDRs and VPC route table changes. Good for high-throughput workloads and predictable latency.
- Private endpoint (AWS PrivateLink style): better isolation, no route table changes in customer VPC but requires ENI-based endpoints and additional cross-account setup. Slightly higher per-connection overhead.

2) CIDR / Ports- Preferred: provide a /24 block for Redwood egress (we can accept peered routes).
- Required outbound: 443 (TLS) to Redwood private endpoint IPs; 123/UDP only if you need NTP (optional).
- If you plan to allow callbacks from our runtime (webhooks), open ports 443 inbound on the private endpoint only.

3) TLS & KMS/HSM- We support end-to-end TLS. By default, Redwood terminates at the private endpoint and maintains TLS to the service runtime. If you require HSM-backed keys, we can integrate with your KMS/HSM via an approved KMS provider (we have existing integrations with AWS KMS and HashiCorp Vault HSM tokens). Please indicate what vendor you plan to use so we can validate compatibility.

4) On‑prem package distribution- We will provide an on-prem package (Docker images + orchestrator manifests) and an inventory PDF. For customers requiring more control, we provide a signed S3 URL with object checksums (sha256) and a timestamped expiry. Dev will prepare the signed link and the checksum file.

5) Preflight checklist (attached)- NAT/firewall rules, hostnames, DNS resolution plan, ACL for management plane, expected concurrency for cache sizing. See attached bordergate_vpc_template.yaml and redwood_onprem_package_inventory.pdf.

- Redwood: SOW draft and high-level timeline (Hannah)
